scope: Bounded inventory-only resolution of the six Papuan Majelis Rakyat bodies explicitly flagged in the Indonesia regional inventory; no streams, metadata validation, EPG, rights or publication.
decision_method: First-level and autonomous special-status legislatures require substantive territorial legislative authority with financial/executive-control functions. Special rights-consent institutions are assessed on their actual allocation, not their titles, Indigenous identity, election process or meeting style.

shared_legal_findings.current_statute: UU 2/2021 replaces Articles 1, 5, 7 and 20. DPRP plus the governor form provincial government; MRP is a distinct cultural representation of Indigenous Papuans. The Act places both in each provincial capital and assigns DPRP provincial enactment, APBD and general supervision. Article 20 retains MRP consideration/consent to Perdasus and specified rights-sensitive matters.
shared_legal_findings.consent_is_real: PP 54/2004 Article 38 provides the Perdasus consideration/consent procedure, including its deemed-consent period; the provincial government and DPRP enact the resulting Perdasus. MRP is not reduced to a voluntary advisory body.
shared_legal_findings.finance_and_scrutiny: PP 54/2004 Articles 42–44 permit rights-related information/reconsideration requests and submission of MRP's own institutional spending to DPRP; that is distinct from approving the province's APBD. Internal rules/decisions under Articles 45/54 are not a general territorial legislative grant.
shared_legal_findings.territorial_relationship: PP 54/2004 Article 74 provides for MRP in successor provinces. The six named current provincial institutions are separately corroborated; the report neither merges them nor duplicates their existing DPRP rows.
shared_legal_findings.currentness: The 2021 statute supersedes older nomination text; PP 64/2008 alters financial provisions. PP 106/2021 preserves non-conflicting prior rules under Article 103. Its 2025 amendment changes development-steering governance, not the MRP legislative allocation.
shared_legal_findings.classification_inference: Outside_default_scope is the project's functional catalogue judgement under its chosen legislative-authority rule, not a denial of the institutions' legal significance or a universal constitutional label.

pp_2008.title: PP 64/2008: Amendment of PP 54/2004

access_and_version_limits: National legal/BPKP/DPR copies of UU 2/2021 encountered timeouts or inaccessible responses. The observed official MRP viewer linked a public PDF that was successfully downloaded and locally extracted instead; a web-reader failure was not treated as missing law.
PP 106/2021 national-reader timeouts and one normal local HTTPS protocol error were resolved through the observed official MRP direct download. Its PDF was directly read through the web reader.

Papua Pegunungan own root and article returned empty direct-reader text. Its primary search index is identified explicitly as the identity evidence method; this is not claimed as full direct article inspection.
No all-member, election, continuous-sitting or every-amendment-to-provincial-Perdasus certification is made. Those are unnecessary to settle this bounded statutory authority allocation.
The old MRP Papua Tengah powers page retains a superseded MPR-delegate provision. It is evidence of a source-version problem, not of a current additional parliamentary function.
